MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL  OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE

  Monday, November 16, 2020

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID- 19 Virus, Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends requirements of the Brown Act. The Council Chambers was closed to the public. The
  La Verne City Council Members attended this meeting telephonically, and the meeting was live streamed on the
  City' s website.

2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6: 30 pm.
3.  Council  Members  present:  Mayor  Tim  Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Robin Carder
  Council  Member Muir Davis
  Council Member Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory  personnel  present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  Assistant to the City Manager JR Ranells
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella

4.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Hepburn.

 5.  Announcements  of  Upcoming  Mayor Hepburn called for public announcements and waited for staff to check
  Community  Events  for any announcements  via telephone  communication.

  One phone call from Sherry Best, President of the La Verne Historical Society
  announcing the release of new historical book titled" La Verne" written by
  La Verne Historian Bill Lemon. Residents can meet the author on Saturday,
  December 5, 2020, at Kuns Park, 10 am to 2 pm.

 6.  Consent  Calendar  It was moved by Davis seconded by Carder and unanimously carried to
  accept, approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items.

  City Council  Minutes  City Council Minutes of November 2, 2020, received and filed.

  Register  of  Audited  Demands  Register of Audited Demands in the amount of$ 1, 091, 718. 49 dated October
  29,  2020.

  Interim Finance Director Alvarado recommended  approval of the above
  Register of Audited Demands.  Approved.

  Youth  and  Family Action  Youth and Familv Action Committee  Executive Board Re- appointment-
  Committee  Executive  Board  The bylaws of the Youth and Family Action Committee( YFAC) allow for a five—
  board that is appointed by City Council. Each  I
  member executive goveming
  Re- appointment
  member serves two- year terms. Board Member Carolyn Cockrell' s term has
  and  she  has  agreed  to  serve  another  two- year term  on  the Committee.
  expired
   City Council Minutes, Monday, November 16, 2020, Page 2

  The Community Services Director recommended that the City Council approve
  the re- appointment of Carolyn Cockrell as member- at- large to the La Verne
  Youth and Family Action Committee for an additional two- year term through
  June 30, 2022. Approved.

  Tri- City Mental  Health  Tri- Citv Mental Health Governinq Board Representative re-appointment-
  Governing Board  The Tri- City Mental Health Governing Board includes one appointment from
  Representative Re- appointment  each City as a community representative.  Carolyn Cockrell has served in this
  capacity since 2011, and has agreed to serve an additional two- year term.

  The Community Services Director recommended that the Council approve the
  re- appointment of Carolyn Cockrell as the community representative from
  La Verne to the Tri- City Mental Health Governing Board to serve a two- year
  term through June 30, 2022. Approved.

  Mayor Pro Tem Carder and Council Member Davis recognized and thanked
  Carolyn Cockrell for her continued willingness to serve on the committees
  representing the City of La Verne.

7.  At 6: 36 pm, the City Council recessed to meet as the Public Financing Authority and reconvened to regular
  session at 6: 58 pm.

S.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Hepburn called for
  public comment and waited for staff to check for any public comment via
  telephone  communication.

  Telephone communications from the following La Verne residents. For
  further information on what was said during public comment, please visit
  the City' s website at cityoflaverne. org and watch the video of the Council
  meeting.

  Gary Hunter
  Terry Prentice
  Kathy Kalousek
  Linda Wilkinson
  Richard Bowen

  Zachary Gibson

  Two public comments  received via email ( attached).

9.  Council Comments  Council Member Crosby wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving and urged
  residents to stay safe especially now with the rise of COVID- 19.
  Council Member Davis wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving, he urged
  residents to stay safe and thanked those who voted in the November 3, 2020
  Election.

  Mayor Pro Tem Carder stated that there were many things to be thankful for
  this Thanksgiving and urged residents to reach out to neighbors and families in
  need. She reported that Sowing Seeds for Life need volunteers to help
  distribute  food.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, November 16, 2020, Page 3

  Council Member Lau wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving and a Happy
  Diwali. She urged residents to stay safe. She reported that the University of
  La Verne is holding a virtual golf tournament and the information on the event
  is on the University' s website.

  Mayor Hepburn thanked the City Council for their dedication and service to the
  community. He also thanked City staff for their hard work in preparing staff
  reports to assist Council in their decision- making. He reported attending a
  Knights of Columbus Mass for the Armed Forces Event celebrating Merchant
  Marines. He spoke about running after a 110- pound tortoise which was
  walking down his street. He wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving and to
  reach out to family and friends.

10.  Adjournment at 7: 16 pm to meet again on Monday, December 7, 2020 at 5: 00 pm for a study session on District
  Voting.

  Respectfully submitted,

  Lupe Gaeta Estrella, CMC

  Please contact LVHS President Sherry Best at sbest@lavernehistoricalsocietv. or or 909/ 596- 4679 to reserve a time to
  make your purchase. A flyer is attached. Support your city and do some holiday shopping at this safe and socially-
  distanced event.

  Sherry Best, President
